commands.name: main.py
commands.description: InvestYo Quant Platform — advisory pipeline launcher

options.name: --interval
options.description: Refresh market data every N seconds (0 = run once and exit).

options.name: --refresh-account
options.description: Force a fresh Robinhood fetch on this launch (bypasses daily cache).

options.name: --agent
options.description: Run the autonomous advisory agent loop: adaptive cadence based on market hours / VIX / regime, backlog reminders for high-conviction signals the operator has not yet logged a decision for, persistent state across restarts.  Takes precedence over --interval.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Log intended orders but do not submit to broker.

options.name: --strict
options.description: Treat DashboardSchema validation failures as fatal (exit 1). For CI / schema-drift gating.

options.name: --date
options.description: As-of date in YYYY-MM-DD format

options.name: --report
options.description: Print survivorship bias report

commands.name: app_shell.py
commands.description: InvestYo native desktop supervisor (UI server + advisory engine loop).

options.name: --interval
options.description: Advisory engine refresh cadence in seconds (default: 300).

options.name: --activate
options.description: Activate the global kill switch.

options.name: --deactivate
options.description: Deactivate the global kill switch.

options.name: --activate-soft-halt
options.description: Activate soft halt (block BUYs).

options.name: --deactivate-soft-halt
options.description: Deactivate soft halt.

options.name: --status
options.description: Print current status.

options.name: --reason
options.description: Reason text (--activate / --activate-soft-halt).

options.name: --strategy
options.description: Name of a single strategy to validate

options.name: --strategies
options.description: Comma-separated OPTIONS strategy names to validate in bulk. Only names registered in validation.options_harness.STANDARD_OPTIONS_STRATEGIES are supported here -- for equity/cross-sectional strategies use `python -m scripts.refresh_validations --strategies ...` instead.

options.name: --start
options.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD)

options.name: --end
options.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD)

options.name: --ticker
options.description: Ticker for options strategy validation

options.name: --workers
options.description: Number of concurrent workers for bulk (--strategies) validation (default: 1 for sequential).

options.name: --json
options.description: In bulk mode, also print ONE machine-readable JSON line (the LAST line of stdout) mapping strategy name -> {deployable, pbo, dsr, sharpe, max_drawdown[, error]}. The human pass/fail table is still printed above it.

commands.name: prompt_registry
commands.description: Prompt Registry — versioned, cryptographically-signed AI prompts.

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.description: Table of prompt IDs with pinned / remote-latest / newest-cached versions.

options.name: --version
options.description: Specific version (e.g. 1.0.0 or 'baseline'). Default: full resolution chain.

options.name: --raw
options.description: Suppress the header comment line — print body text only.

subcommands.name: sync
subcommands.description: Fetch the remote manifest and pre-warm the disk cache.

subcommands.name: pin
subcommands.description: Pin a prompt ID to a specific version.

subcommands.name: rollback
subcommands.description: Roll back to the previous cached version.

subcommands.name: diff
subcommands.description: Unified diff between two versions of a prompt.

subcommands.name: verify
subcommands.description: Re-check signatures and guardrails for cached versions.

positionals.name: id
positionals.description: Specific prompt ID (default: all known IDs).

subcommands.name: publish
subcommands.description: Sign a file and push it to the remote store (publish credentials required).

options.name: --version
options.description: Version string to publish (e.g. 1.1.0).

options.name: --author
options.description: Author identifier.

options.name: --notes
options.description: Changelog note.

positionals.name: file
positionals.description: Path to the file containing the prompt body.

options.name: --json
options.description: Output machine-readable JSON array instead of a human-readable table

options.name: --skip
options.description: Skip named checks (e.g. --skip heartbeat_fresh paper_trading_duration). Useful in CI where certain checks are contextually inapplicable.

options.name: --fire-alerts
options.description: Dispatch a CRITICAL alert via observability.alerts.send_alert when validation_reports fails. Off by default so an interactive run never pages anyone; intended for a scheduled/CI invocation of this script.

options.name: --validation-staleness-only
options.description: Run ONLY the validation_reports check (strategy backtest staleness and deployability), bypassing the ADVISORY_ONLY auto-skip that applies to the full go-live gate, and always firing an alert on FAIL (fire_alert=True). Intended for a daily scheduled cron invocation independent of the go-live gate below — strategy health is worth monitoring whether or not the platform is submitting live orders. Ignores --skip and --fire-alerts.

commands.name: refresh_validations.py

options.name: --strategies

options.name: --start
options.description: Backtest start date (default: 2005-01-01).

options.name: --end
options.description: Backtest end date (default: today).

options.name: --output-dir
options.description: Directory for JSON report output (default: reports/).

options.name: --n-cpcv-splits
options.description: Number of CPCV splits (default: 10).

options.name: --n-test-splits
options.description: Walk-forward test splits (default: 2).

options.name: --workers
options.description: Number of concurrent workers for strategy validation (default: 1 for sequential). See run_validations()'s docstring for the profiled lgbm_ranker/LightGBM thread-oversubscription caveat (measured negligible on a 10-core machine as of 2026-08-14).

options.name: --json
options.description: Also print ONE machine-readable JSON line (the LAST line of stdout) mapping strategy_id → {deployable, pbo, dsr, sharpe, max_drawdown, universe_coverage_pct, universe_coverage_ok[, error]}. The human pass/fail table is still printed above it.

options.name: --output-dir
options.description: Directory containing state_snapshot.json, dead_letter.json, history/. Default: ./output

options.name: --print
options.description: Also print the briefing to stdout after writing the file.

commands.name: track_record_status.py
commands.description: Report InvestYo paper-trading track-record progress (90-day gate, calibration depth/coverage, last-run staleness).

options.name: --output-dir
options.description: Directory containing decision_log.jsonl, heartbeat.txt, state_snapshot.json. Default: ./output

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of the human-readable report.

commands.description: InvestYo database schema setup -- CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS against quant_platform.db, driven by config.COLUMN_SCHEMA. Idempotent; additive migrations only (never drops/alters destructively).

commands.name: repair_price_bars_adjustment.py
commands.description:
CLI remediation script for a bars-adjustment-convention mismatch already persisted into
`price_bars` (e.g. FMP_BARS_ADJUSTMENT was set to 'full'/'light' — split-only — instead of the
correct 'dividend-adjusted' convention for a period of time, or any future provider/config
change that similarly splices two adjustment conventions into one (symbol, date) series).

Where to add symbols for this process: the --tickers argument below. This is the durable,
discoverable home for that — not a hardcoded list in this script, and not a one-off inline
command. See --help for the three ways to specify a ticker set.

What it does per symbol
------------------------
1. Finds the earliest date in `price_bars` written under --source (default 'fmpprovider') --
   i.e. the first date that could have been fetched under the bad adjustment convention.
2. Deletes ALL rows for that symbol from that date forward (any source, not just --source) --
   the safe choice, because price_bars is keyed by (symbol, date) and a stale row from another
   source sitting inside the affected window would leave the same adjustment-convention splice
   the cleanup is meant to remove. Rows strictly BEFORE the first affected date are left alone
   (genuinely unaffected history is not thrown away just because the symbol also has some FMP
   rows).
3. Calls HistoricalStore.get_bars(symbol), which re-fetches from whatever provider chain is
   CURRENTLY configured (settings.MARKET_DATA_PROVIDER / FMP_BARS_ADJUSTMENT) via its existing
   incremental-top-up logic -- filling exactly the gap just opened, no bespoke date-range-fetch
   code needed.

If a symbol has no rows from --source at all, it's skipped (nothing to repair) and reported
separately -- never silently treated as "processed".

Never raises out of the per-symbol loop (dead-letter resilience, matching every other backfill
script in scripts/) -- one bad symbol does not abort the batch.

options.name: --tickers
options.description: Comma-separated ticker list (e.g. 'AAPL,MSFT'), 'universe' for the operator's tracked universe (held ∪ watchlists ∪ DEFAULT_TICKERS, via resolve_universe), or 'all' for every symbol currently carrying a --source row in price_bars.

options.name: --random
options.description: Add this many additional random symbols (from every symbol carrying a --source row in price_bars) on top of --tickers. Skips symbols already selected.

options.name: --source
options.description: price_bars.source value that identifies the affected rows (default: 'fmpprovider').

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Report what would be deleted/re-fetched per symbol without touching the DB.
